newsitem.title: USA: Warner-Lambert gains after panel backs drug.
newsitem.headline: Warner-Lambert gains after panel backs drug.

text.p: Shares in Warner-Lambert Co rose in late trading after a U.S. Food and Drug Administration advisory panel voted to recommend the agency approve its drug for treating type II diabetes.
The panel voted unanimously to back the drug, with the brand name Rezulin. The FDA is not bound to advisory panel recommendations but typically follows them.

"This a major, major milestone," said David Saks at Gruntal & Go. The stock rose 1-1/4 to a session high of 74-1/2 shortly after the panel vote. It settled up 3/8 at 73-5/8 in later trading, but was up from the day's low at 71-1/4.

The drug was discovered by Sankyo Co Ltd and licensed by Warner-Lambert in the United States, Canada and Mexico. Glaxo Wellcome Plc has licensed the drug, with the generic name troglitazone, in Europe.
Analysts estimate Warner-Lambert could have sales of the drug of around $500 million a year by the year 2000.

Industry analysts see the diabetes drug as a key driver of the future growth of Warner-Lambert's pharmaceutical business, along with the cholesterol-lowering drug atorvastatin, which has been filed for FDA review.
